public_rationale: The May 27, 2025 preprint evaluated code execution across 144 reasoning and planning tasks, including logic, spatial reasoning, optimization, search, and mathematics [e1]. On 37 held-out task types, GPT-4o scored 58.6% with text-only reasoning and 70.9% with Code Interpreter [e1]. This within-model comparison supports the qualified claim that combining neural models with executable operations helps across several kinds of tasks [e1].
limitations: The evidence comes from one preprint and selected benchmarks; it does not establish how frequently tools help across real-world tasks [e1].
The R1-CI comparisons change training as well as tool access, limiting attribution of those gains to tools alone [e1].
The performance comparison does not settle whether this combination should be called neurosymbolic AI.

statement.excerpt: Systems that draw on code interpreter, and hence by definition are neurosymbolic, often outperform those that lack symbolic tools, at least in a bunch of tasks. This is confirmation of the value of neurosymbolic AI.
statement.document_title: How o3 and Grok 4 Accidentally Vindicated Neurosymbolic AI

our_interpretation: The plain reading is repeated performance gains across several kinds of tasks, not superiority on every task.
I assess contemporary systems during 2025 through the post date. This year-to-date window represents the current benchmark reporting period; this field has no standard quarterly reporting cycle.

I use Marcus's broad meaning of neurosymbolic: a neural model combined with executable symbolic operations. The assessment concerns the usefulness of that combination, not whether this terminology is universally accepted.
Comparable evaluations should include text-only baselines. Comparisons between different models alone cannot isolate the contribution of tools.
criteria.support_condition: Comparative evaluations show repeated correctness gains across multiple task families when systems use code execution rather than text-only reasoning.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Broad, comparable evaluations show that code-interpreter systems generally lack the claimed repeated advantages across task families.
